text:
How to Optimize Performance in Visual Studio Code

In this developer productivity video, we go over how to optimize performance in Visual Studio Code. We cover topics like selecting a proper working directory, excluding files, disabling extensions, and updating the default settings.json file. Following these tips will make your VS Code run faster. 📖 Code - https://github.com/SuboptimalEng/dotfiles 🎥 YouTube - https://youtube.com/SuboptimalEng 💻 GitHub - https://github.com/SuboptimalEng 🐦 Twitter - https://twitter.com/SuboptimalEng 🧵 Threads - https://www.threads.net/@suboptimaleng 📸 Instagram - https://instagram.com/suboptimaleng == [ Resources ] == VS Code Performance Tips: https://betterprogramming.pub/5-tips-to-boost-the-performance-of-your-vs-code-editor-ff28dda68d9b == [ Timestamps ] == 00:00 Working Directory Setup 00:54 Exclude Node Modules 01:24 Remove Unused Extensions 02:03 Bracket Pair Colorizer 03:13 Update VS Code Defaults 03:36 Hide Editor Minimap 04:05 Disable Search on Type 04:42 Terminal GPU Acceleration 04:56 Disable Code Lens 05:21 Outro == [ Tags ] == #suboptimal #vscode #visualstudio

plan.title: Optimize Performance in Visual Studio Code
plan.summary: A set of VS Code tuning steps covering working directory setup, excluding files, disabling extensions and features, and editing settings.json to make the editor run faster.

moves.title: Update your settings.json defaults
moves.intent: Apply the performance-oriented defaults to settings.json so VS Code starts and runs faster.

moves.title: Exclude node_modules from VS Code
moves.intent: Add node_modules to VS Code's file watcher and search exclusions in an existing project.

moves.title: Remove unused extensions
moves.intent: Uninstall or disable extensions that aren't actively used to cut startup and runtime overhead.

moves.title: Turn off minimap, search-on-type and Code Lens; enable terminal GPU acceleration
moves.intent: Flip the specific settings for hiding the minimap, disabling search-as-you-type, disabling Code Lens, and turning on terminal GPU acceleration.
